query: What goal-management practices support high achievement?

per_column.name: goal_specificity_score
per_column.rationale: Specificity of a goal is a genuine constitutive aspect of good goal-management practice (the 'S' in SMART), an aspect OF how well goals are managed.

per_column.name: has_quantified_target
per_column.rationale: Whether a goal has a measurable/quantified target is a constitutive facet of goal-management quality (measurability), an aspect of the practice itself.

per_column.name: goal_duration_days
per_column.rationale: Time-bounding/duration is a constitutive facet of goal setting (the 'T' in SMART), an aspect of how the goal is framed rather than an external predictor.

per_column.name: priority_numeric
per_column.rationale: Prioritization is a legitimate aspect of goal-management practice; however it is a numeric restatement of the existing 'priority' column, adding little new facet coverage.

per_column.name: achievement_vs_target
per_column.rationale: This measures achievement/outcome, i.e., the high achievement the practices are supposed to SUPPORT. It is the dependent outcome, not a facet of the management practices themselves.

per_column.name: goal_outcome
per_column.rationale: Final completion status is the achievement outcome, not a constitutive part of the success-factor practices; it also overlaps heavily with achievement_vs_target.

judge.rationale: The concept is the set of goal-management PRACTICES that support achievement. Genuine facets present cover SMART-style dimensions: specificity, measurability (quantified target), and time-bounding (duration). Priority is a facet but duplicates the existing priority column. Mutual exclusivity is weakened by two pairs of overlaps: priority_numeric restates priority, and achievement_vs_target overlaps with goal_outcome. Critically, two of the six added columns (achievement_vs_target, goal_outcome) are the achievement OUTCOME the practices are meant to drive, not facets of the practices themselves, violating the part-of requirement. Exhaustiveness is low because key management-practice facets (ownership/accountability, relevance/alignment, tracking/update cadence, realistic attainability) are absent, and the only genuine facets are a partial SMART subset.
